newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand crop forecast likely down on floods.
newsitem.headline: Thailand crop forecast likely down on floods.

text.p: The Thai Agriculture Ministry was likely to revise down current projections for rice and soybean output due to flood damage but keep that for sugarcane steady, a ministry official said Friday.
Monthol Chiamcharoen, of the ministry's forecast division, said crop damage by floods this year was less severe than that of last year, when the worst flooding in 50 years hit Thailand.
"On soybean, based on our officials' reports from major soybean growing provinces, it seems that the damage is not as bad as many might anticipate," he told Reuters.
The ministry revises crop data every second month. The latest report will be released by next week, Monthol added.

The previous forecast put the first crop rice output for the 1996/97 (April-March) crop year at 18.11 million tonnes, corn (July-June) at 4.36 million tonnes, soybean (April-March) at 411,916 tonnes and sugarcane (Nov-Oct) at 62.42 million tonnes.
Monthol noted the data was gathered before the flood situation deteriorated in some areas in recent weeks and might not reflect the true extent of the damage.
"We will go ahead and release the data as scheduled and I will probably write a follow-up report on the latest damage later," he said.
